genericProblem: A backend-acceptance implementation can pass static admission while its managed runtime evidence loses the sender and lifecycle facts required to explain a terminal signal, and while its package-exit denominator remains wholly unclosed. Retrying a focused child process then consumes time without producing an admissible full four-dimension verdict.

finiteDenominator.scope: Every detached catalog workload child and its remote managed wrapper in backend-acceptance.
Every focused or full backend-acceptance run whose final receipt must retain admission order, child first failure, last known good boundary, and cleanup independently.
All 196 current semantic operations after the P0/W0/P1 check correctly promotes current changes to ALL.
The complete current 196-operation provider, scenario, receipt, baseline, and historical-replay denominator.
All runtime and test-support BA-U step identifiers; doc/evidence/review/gate-catalog metadata are explicit counterexamples.
The local public orchestration process, the managed remote shell, and every Docker-backed Gradle JVM guarded by V2S_TESTCONTAINERS_EXECUTION_PLANE.
Every backend-acceptance admission from public CLI through the current remote daemon status manifest to its isolated lane and writable namespace plan.
Every managed SIGTERM trace whose sender is external to the run-owned process tree, plus the fixed remote systemd, cron and active terminator-process denominator.
Every backend-acceptance monitored child where raw artifact writes, terminal-result collection, resource cleanup, and semantic HTTP completion have distinct meanings.
Every parent runner parsing a child heartbeat, including legacy CURRENT/TOTAL and managed r5 CURRENT/COMPLETED/TOTAL records.

counterexamples.boundary: Static self-tests and standards coverage prove mechanical controls, not sender attribution or a fresh four-dimension dynamic verdict.
A named 1/196 catalog operation may provide local regression evidence but cannot close the 196-operation ledger, accepted baseline, historical replay, or package exit.
A PASS for declared process, scratch, container, and volume cleanup cannot offset a business failure, lost first-failure receipt, or an unattributed signal.
A null supervisor signal and empty dispatch list exclude the recorded supervisor path only; they do not identify the remote OS or external sender.

findings.genericProblem: Terminal child signals are receiver-only evidence, so a repeated SIGTERM cannot be attributed to a sender or causal process tree.
evidence: backend-acceptance-1786618913661-9dde6383 firstFailure=BACKEND_ACCEPTANCE_CATALOG_CHILD_SIGNAL_SIGTERM
backend-acceptance-1786619640901-1d44700d firstFailure=BACKEND_ACCEPTANCE_CATALOG_CHILD_SIGNAL_SIGTERM
catalog child outcome records supervisorSignal=null, forwardedSignals=[], and signalDispatches=[]
findings.minimalRepair: Create a run-owned, script-managed remote signal trace with receiver and sender identity, preserve it with the child outcome, and fail a terminal signal as UNATTRIBUTED_SIGNAL when the trace cannot establish provenance.

findings.genericProblem: The final runner manifest is rebuilt from the pre-start manifest and the remote bridge flattens a schema-bearing child failure, losing required admission ordering and broken-boundary facts.
evidence: tools/backend-acceptance/runner.mjs marks container initialization in startedManifest but builds finished from manifest
backend-acceptance-1786619640901-1d44700d run-manifest has containerInitializationStartedAt=null and childWorkload=null
scripts/test/r5-remote-testcontainers.mjs converts a nonzero backend-acceptance Gradle result to REMOTE_TEST_OR_CONTAINER_CLEANUP_FAILED
findings.minimalRepair: Carry one current manifest through completion and validate/map the backend-acceptance child receipt without lossy error folding; add red mutations for timestamp loss and child-boundary loss.

findings.genericProblem: Production-surface changes correctly produce ALL impact but no machine-valid change disposition exists for the resulting 196-operation denominator.
evidence: scripts/check/backend-acceptance-change-impact --package-exit returns BACKEND_ACCEPTANCE_CHANGE_DISPOSITIONS_MISSING
P0=633, P1=633, and 14 changed P1 paths are outside W0, so impactMode=ALL is correct
findings.minimalRepair: Do not weaken impact derivation; generate and validate complete, source-backed dispositions only as each affected operation obtains its required scenario/regression or fresh behavior-unchanged proof.

findings.genericProblem: The static registry creates 196 providers but has migrated none of the 196 operations to a measured, receipt-backed dynamic baseline.
evidence: preflight reports OPERATIONS=196, PROVIDERS=196, KNOWN_UNCOVERED_OPEN=196, KNOWN_UNCOVERED_COVERED=0, BASELINE_MEASURED=0, DYNAMIC=NOT_CLOSED
historical replay denominator remains 6 PERFORMANCE + 15 HTTP + 8 NON_ROUTE
findings.minimalRepair: After signal/receipt repair, migrate owner-derived scenarios in finite owner batches; each batch needs source reread, route red/green, fresh four-dimension receipt, historical disposition, and ledger removal only when justified.

findings.genericProblem: Step identifiers appear in runtime and test-support source even though only evidence and gate metadata may carry journey/step names.
evidence: tools/backend-acceptance/cli.mjs references BA-U01 through BA-U06 in executable source
tools/backend-acceptance/runner.mjs and tools/backend-acceptance/impact.mjs also contain BA-U step identifiers
findings.minimalRepair: Move step labels to manifest or gate-catalog metadata, use capability names in runtime source, and add an admitted red mutation covering the complete runtime/test-support denominator.

findings.genericProblem: A local Node orchestration boundary can incorrectly enforce the remote-JVM Testcontainers opt-in before it launches the managed remote runner, making every public backend-acceptance invocation fail before resource admission or first-failure evidence.
evidence: 2026-08-13 public scripts/test/backend-acceptance --operation preflightOperationsBrandCatalogCopy exited before container initialization with V2S_TESTCONTAINERS_REMOTE_REQUIRED
tools/backend-acceptance/runner.mjs execute called requireManagedPlane(environment) in the local orchestrator
scripts/test/r5-remote-testcontainers.mjs exports V2S_TESTCONTAINERS_EXECUTION_PLANE=remote immediately before remote Gradle, and build.gradle.kts guards Docker-backed Gradle tasks
findings.minimalRepair: Remove the JVM-only guard from the local orchestrator; mechanically prove the local/remote/Gradle three-part boundary, including red mutations for each link.

findings.genericProblem: A public backend-acceptance runner can require a capacity and namespace environment value that no managed entrypoint supplies, failing before it writes an admissible resource manifest or performs the remote preflight required to establish actual isolated capacity.
evidence: 2026-08-13 public scripts/test/backend-acceptance --operation preflightOperationsBrandCatalogCopy passed static admission then failed with BACKEND_ACCEPTANCE_RESOURCE_MAXIMUM_INVALID before container initialization
tools/backend-acceptance/lanes.mjs read V2S_BACKEND_ACCEPTANCE_ISOLATED_RESOURCE_MAXIMUM and V2S_BACKEND_ACCEPTANCE_NAMESPACE_PREFIX directly from an unconfigured caller environment
scripts/test/r5-testcontainers-daemon-lanes.mjs already owns current remote daemon status and writes a run-scoped manifest with distinct daemon engine IDs

Initial PF-07 control red mutation found that daemon-status manifests carry raw socket paths while child environment values carry unix:// URI strings; receipt validation must preserve that schema distinction
findings.minimalRepair: Use the managed daemon-status receipt as the authoritative current resource preflight, validate its raw socket-path schema separately from the child URI environment schema, record it in backend-acceptance admission, derive a run-scoped namespace prefix, permit only a bounded requested lane count, and reject shell overrides of observed capacity or namespace.

findings.genericProblem: A signal trace can record the receiver as its sender and omit the fork/exec lineage needed to distinguish run-owned shutdown from an external terminator; without a bounded remote source/process diagnostic, an observed pkill cannot be governed safely.
evidence: backend-acceptance-1786621821294-edf49294 records raw ftrace pkill-169192 signal_generate comm=node pid=168517
the former parser assigned comm=node to senderComm even though the ftrace task prefix identifies pkill-169192
the former trace captured only signal_generate and the existing daemon diagnosis had no systemd/cron/active-terminator receipt
findings.minimalRepair: Derive sender identity from the ftrace task prefix, preserve receiver separately, capture a run-scoped sched_process_fork lineage filtered to pkill/killall, and extend the existing managed daemon diagnosis with a boot-bound, content-hash-only scan of fixed systemd/cron roots plus active pkill/killall identities.

findings.genericProblem: A monitored backend-acceptance run can treat raw event-file bytes as semantic operation progress, and can then turn a separately proven resource cleanup into CLEANUP FAIL merely because terminal business artifacts were unavailable after a controlled stop.
evidence: backend-acceptance-1786622516349-4ff98616 remained at operation=0 with Gradle log fixed at 10257B while runtimeEvidenceBytes grew
the controlled stop was identity-bound and r5 recorded process/scratch/containers/volumes PASS
r5 firstFailure=REMOTE_RESULT_NOT_AVAILABLE and finalizeCleanupAfterCollection changed cleanup status/reaped to FAIL despite all resource components PASS
findings.minimalRepair: For backend-acceptance use only Gradle/test-result and semantic completed-or-firstFailure state as the stall observation; retain resource cleanup verdict from its component evidence and record artifact collection failure separately as business/evidence failure.

findings.genericProblem: The parent runner can either require adjacent CURRENT and TOTAL fields although the managed r5 child inserts COMPLETED, or accept a malformed interleaved counter without checking that it agrees with CURRENT; either outcome makes live parent progress untrustworthy.
evidence: backend-acceptance-1786622984669-a3c8cb2c runner.jsonl records R5_TESTCONTAINERS_HEARTBEAT CURRENT=1 COMPLETED=1 TOTAL=1 while parent progress remained 0/1 until collection
tools/backend-acceptance/runner.mjs initially parsed only CURRENT=(number) followed immediately by TOTAL=(number), then its optional COMPLETED form accepted a mismatched value
the M-01 red proof executed runner selfTest with CURRENT=1 COMPLETED=0 TOTAL=2 and failed BACKEND_ACCEPTANCE_RUNNER_SELF_TEST_INCONSISTENT_R5_PROGRESS_ACCEPTED
repository-wide protocol scan found parent-owned CURRENT/TOTAL output plus the managed r5 child’s structured CURRENT/COMPLETED/TOTAL emission; no third format was found
findings.minimalRepair: Accept exactly the two known event/layout pairs, require the interleaved COMPLETED value to equal CURRENT, retain total/range guards and first-failure monotonicity, and keep executable red proof for malformed interleaved and unknown layouts.

preventionDispositions.reason: The managed remote wrapper must fail closed when a terminal child signal lacks run-owned provenance evidence.
Receipt continuity is mechanically assertable by static red mutation before a managed run is attempted.
The existing P0/W0/P1 control already promotes uncovered production changes to ALL and must remain fail closed.
No static count or focused run can substitute for owner-source-derived provider migration and fresh full-denominator evidence.
The existing code-layout control owns the runtime/test-support journey naming prohibition and needs a complete-denominator red mutation.
The control binds the local orchestrator, managed remote shell, and Gradle Testcontainers guard, and rejects removal or inversion of any one boundary.
The control rejects capacity and namespace spoofing, unavailable or malformed daemon-status receipts, and any lane count outside the managed daemon denominator.

The controls reject receiver-as-sender parsing, missing filtered fork trace coverage, and unbounded or unparseable remote terminator governance evidence before any host process is considered for action.

Focused red mutations prove that raw event bytes cannot reset a zero-operation stall and that artifact collection failure cannot overwrite independently proven process, scratch, container, or volume cleanup.
The runner self-test has real red proof for a mismatched interleaved counter and now proves both finite source-observed layouts, known event kinds, total/range guards, and first-failure monotonicity.
